report.summary: The write path of the Social Network namespace is failing because the ClusterIP service name 'user-service' does not resolve inside the cluster. compose-post-service logs 'Thrift: ... TSocket::open() getaddrinfo() <Host: user-service Port: 9090> Name or service not known' on every request between 14:38:03 and 14:38:10 (69-78 such lines per 30 s), and nginx-thrift logs 'compose.lua:62: ComposePost(): compost_post failure: Could not resolve host for client socket.' for every POST /wrk2-api/post/compose at the same timestamps. The kube-system/coredns ConfigMap's Corefile contains a template plugin rule that matches '^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\.$' and returns rcode NXDOMAIN, which explains why only that one name fails to resolve while every other service name resolves normally. user-service itself looks functional: its Service (10.96.160.100, created 14:37:43) and endpoint (10.244.125.21:9090) exist, its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, it started its server at 14:37:49 with no error lines, and user-mongodb accepted its connections and built the user.user indexes at 14:37:49. The read path is unaffected in the sampled traces (home-timeline/user-timeline reads returned HTTP 200 in 1.2-4.1 ms). All 27 deployments are 1/1 ready and all 27 pods are Running with 0 restarts; the whole application was freshly created at 14:37:44-14:37:49, so the failures appear from the first compose request. The conclusion is partial because the NXDOMAIN response itself was not directly observed (CoreDNS query logging is off) and the time at which the template rule was added to the ConfigMap cannot be determined.

claims.text: The ConfigMap kube-system/coredns holds a Corefile with a template plugin block: 'template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { match "^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\\.$" rcode NXDOMAIN fallthrough }', i.e. an always-on rule that answers NXDOMAIN for exactly the user-service DNS name.

Both CoreDNS pods (coredns-84479d5769-8l5zk, coredns-84479d5769-p7r96) are Running and loaded a configuration at 14:37:52.971Z and 14:37:53.255Z, logging '[INFO] plugin/reload: Running configuration SHA512 = 0f2c9351...'; the ConfigMap's kubectl last-applied-configuration annotation carries the same user-service NXDOMAIN template block and its creationTimestamp is 2026-11-21T04:08:34Z.

Mechanism: the template rule in the kube-system/coredns Corefile forces NXDOMAIN for user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local, so the getaddrinfo lookup of host 'user-service' inside compose-post-service fails with 'Name or service not known'; every compose request therefore aborts at its first dependency and nginx-thrift returns a compose failure. The rule is the only observed name-resolution failure and it names exactly the host, port and namespace that are failing, while other service names still resolve from pods on the same node.

Rejected: that user-service itself is broken (crash, bad start, or loss of its MongoDB/redis dependencies). Its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, it logged a normal start with no errors, and user-mongodb recorded its connections and successful index builds for user.user.

Rejected: that a missing Service or empty Endpoints object for user-service causes the failure. The Service exists (ClusterIP 10.96.160.100, created 14:37:43Z) and the Endpoints subset already contains 10.244.125.21:9090.

Rejected: that the MongoDB index/connection errors ('Failed to create mongodb index', 'No suitable servers found ... serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired' from social-graph-service, user-timeline-service and url-shorten-service at 14:37:45-14:37:50) are this incident. They are startup retries while the mongodb pods were still booting, and user-timeline-service later executed 'user_timeline_mongo_find_client' spans of 8-23 us inside the successful read traces.

Counter-evidence against a general DNS or node-network outage: only compose-post-service logs getaddrinfo failures in the whole namespace, while pods on the same node sregym-worker (home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service) resolved and called services on other nodes successfully inside the sampled read traces.

gaps: The NXDOMAIN DNS response itself was not observed: CoreDNS does not enable query logging, so the link between the Corefile template rule and the getaddrinfo failure is inferred from the rule content plus the client-side 'Name or service not known' error for exactly host user-service:9090.

Cannot determine when the user-service NXDOMAIN template block was added to ConfigMap kube-system/coredns: its creationTimestamp is 2026-11-21T04:08:34Z (before the authorized window), the last-applied-configuration annotation already contains the block, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

No application-level Prometheus series were available for these services: get_metric_names for {__name__=~".+"} returned only node-exporter, cadvisor, kube-state-metrics and Prometheus self-metrics, and queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no series, so error-rate and latency metrics for compose-post-service, user-service and nginx-thrift could not be checked; missing series are unknown, not zero.

The HTTP status returned to clients for the failing compose requests is unknown: traces_search_by_tags on nginx-web-server with tag http.status_code="500" and with error=true returned no traces, and the compose operations never appear in the sampled traces.
A query for NetworkPolicies in namespace social-network returned no objects (status no_data), so by a citable ok view I cannot confirm whether a policy intervenes; no policy object was observed.

Log history is limited: Loki returned error lines only from ~14:37:45 onward and a query on {namespace="social-network", app="nginx-web-server"} for 10:00-12:00Z returned nothing, so the pre-deployment state of the cluster and of the read/write paths is unknown.

Scope of other callers of user-service is unknown: user-mention-service logged only a single startup line with no request activity, and the compose path aborts at its first dependency, so it is unverified whether any other service was affected by the user-service name-resolution failure.

The actual DNS resolver behavior from the compose-post-service pod (e.g. resolv.conf, nodelocal DNS cache) could not be inspected directly, so whether the template rule is the sole resolution blocker versus one of several is not fully verified.
next_steps: Have a human remove the NXDOMAIN template block for user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local from the kube-system/coredns Corefile (or restore the previous Corefile) and confirm CoreDNS reloads cleanly.

After the change, verify from a social-network pod that 'user-service' resolves to 10.96.160.100 and that POST /wrk2-api/post/compose returns success; re-check compose-post-service logs for the getaddrinfo error.

Audit cluster change history / kubectl apply records for ConfigMap kube-system/coredns to establish when and by whom the template rule was introduced (change_history integration is not available in this Run).
Consider enabling CoreDNS query logging or a DNS-failure alert so that resolver-level faults are directly observable in future incidents.
